摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

From knowledge retrieval to generation: a comprehensive study of RAG's architectures, evolution, and applications

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11716-1 · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning, but their reliance on static parametric knowledge still leads to knowledge staleness, hallucinations, limited domain adaptability, weak traceability, and high updating costs in knowledge-intensive scenarios. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps address these limitations by incorporating external knowledge sources into the generation process, making it an important approach for improving factual grounding, knowledge timeliness, and evidence traceability. However, existing RAG research is increasingly fragmented across architectures, retrieval and generation strategies, evaluation methods, application scenarios, deployment constraints, and security risks. To provide a systematic understanding of this field, this survey reviews RAG research through a structured and transparent review protocol. We organize the review around three major dimensions: the system stack and paradigm evolution of RAG, evaluation methods and application evidence, and practical deployment and security challenges. Specifically, we analyze the core components of RAG systems, synthesize their evolution from Naive RAG to Agentic RAG, examine evaluation metrics and stress-testing protocols, summarize benchmark datasets and domain applications, and discuss deployment constraints and emerging risks such as prompt injection, data poisoning, retrieval hijacking, privacy leakage, and citation laundering. This survey provides a taxonomy-oriented, evaluation-aware, and deployment-conscious reference for understanding the development, limitations, and future directions of RAG systems.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Towards efficient large language models for scientific data: a review

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11727-y · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

The adaptation of large language models (LLMs) to scientific domains requires efficient strategies to mitigate high computational costs while preserving performance. We present a systematic survey of efficiency techniques for adapting LLMs to scientific applications. Our review analyzes 120 studies across seven scientific fields, including biomedicine, clinical medicine, biology, mathematics, chemistry, geo-environmental science, and cross-domain scientific research. Across the surveyed literature, we summarize 34 representative models and 30 scientific datasets for efficient scientific LLM research. Examining parameter-efficient fine-tuning, knowledge distillation, architectural optimization, and data-centric approaches, we introduce a dual-axis taxonomy that organizes efficiency techniques by both methodological strategy and scientific domain. We further provide practical guidance for selecting efficiency strategies under resource constraints and highlight open challenges including multimodal integration, catastrophic forgetting, and automated method selection. By synthesizing cross-domain evidence and outlining directions for sustainable model development, this survey supports the adoption of efficient scientific LLMs in resource-constrained research environments and promotes more accessible and responsible deployment across scientific disciplines.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Seeing ahead through a state-of-the-art review of visual perception and predictive intelligence for collaborative robots

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11708-1 · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

The rate at which collaborative robots (cobots) are evolving from isolated, pre-programmed manipulators into collaborative partners that operate productively alongside humans, other robots, and machines is accelerating rapidly. Advances in computer vision is enabling cobots, even in dynamic and cluttered settings, to detect, recognise and assess both environment and actions. However, achieving higher detection accuracy and real-time localization in dynamic systems remains a challenge, as most existing approaches assume uncluttered backgrounds with limited scene complexity. Closing this gap is critical for both research and industrial deployment. This paper reviews the development of visual perception in cobots, surveys emerging computer vision algorithms, and examines a holistic perception pipeline in which raw vision signals, vision language models (VLMs), and augmented/virtual reality interfaces jointly power a unified sense-think-act loop. The review finds that cobots in high-mix, reconfigurable factories face serious challenges: occlusions in fields of view, fluctuating illumination, ambiguous backgrounds, few- or zero-shot object scenarios, high-speed motion, and computational problems in fusing heterogeneous data streams in real time. Cobots also need to manipulate damaged items, requiring vision algorithms that infer geometry from sparse cues and support adaptive grasping. Finally, the review identifies three complementary research directions to unlock plug-and-play cobots: (1) information aware sensor-fusion pipelines transmitting only credible voxels to reduce bandwidth while preserving sub-millimetre accuracy; (2) language conditioned planning and control networks mapping plain-language goals to smooth, jerk-bounded trajectories; and (3) pre-trained few-shot reward heads that score task progress without bespoke metrics, closing the reinforcement learning (RL) loop. Combined, these advances promise cobots that can be commissioned with relatively few demonstrations.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Adaptation of foundation models in medical image analysis: mechanisms, evidence, and deployment considerations

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11733-0 · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

Foundation models, pretrained on diverse data, objectives, or modalities for reuse across downstream tasks, are increasingly applied to medical image analysis. Their performance depends not only on pretraining but also on how they are adapted to specific tasks, data regimes, and deployment settings. Whereas previous reviews have considered adaptation within broader syntheses, this review focuses specifically on post-pretraining interventions applied to existing FMs. Using a structured narrative review with a systematic, auditable workflow, we identified 719 eligible reports representing 705 independent studies. Of these, 473 provided controlled comparative evidence: 322 formally published studies formed the primary synthesis and 151 preprint-only studies a sensitivity layer. Adaptation was organized into five non-mutually exclusive families: parameter-level, representation-level, objective-level, data-centric, and architectural/sequence-level adaptation, with model use and update regime analyzed separately. Controlled comparisons showed no consistent ranking among frozen, parameter-efficient, partial, or full updating, or across broader adaptation families; outcomes varied by task, data regime, comparator, and evaluation setting. Clinical-readiness evidence remained limited: 173/705 studies (24.5%) had confirmed independent external validation, 10 (1.4%) reported calibration or uncertainty evidence, and 97/322 formally published comparative studies (30.1%) included a qualifying externally validated arm. Overall, FM adaptation is a context-dependent design space rather than a hierarchy of preferred strategies.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Explaining teacher adoption of AI through the technology acceptance model: a meta-analysis and systematic review

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11736-x · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education has accelerated rapidly, yet the factors shaping teachers’ adoption of these technologies remain insufficiently understood. A growing body of empirical research applies the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to examine how teachers integrate AI, focusing on perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEOU), and behavioral intention (BI). TAM was, however, originally developed for static, deterministic technologies, and AI differs in its opacity, adaptivity, and capacity to challenge professional roles and identity, raising the question of whether perceived usefulness and ease of use alone are sufficient to predict adoption intentions in this context. Following PRISMA guidelines, this study conducts a systematic review of 38 empirical studies ( N = 15,919 teachers across 19 countries) on teachers’ AI adoption, together with a meta-analysis of the subset reporting extractable bivariate correlations. A random-effects model (DerSimonian–Laird) is used to estimate the associations among PEOU, PU, and BI across k = 24 studies ( N = 11,768 ), while the full corpus is synthesised to identify contextual conditions shaping these relationships. Pooled correlations are positive and moderate to strong (PEOU–PU: r = 0.532 , 95% CI [0.410, 0.636]; PEOU–BI: r = 0.536 , 95% CI [0.435, 0.623]; PU–BI: r = 0.619 , 95% CI [0.511, 0.708]), and are robust to alternative variance estimators and to the inclusion of UTAUT studies under a construct-equivalence ruling. Heterogeneity is very high ( I² = 97.9% – 98.6% ) and prediction intervals span from negative to near-unity values, indicating that these associations hold directionally but vary considerably across contexts in ways the core model does not represent. Egger’s regression indicates funnel asymmetry on all three associations; leave-one-out diagnostics attribute this asymmetry entirely to a single large-sample, low-effect study, and the asymmetry is not interpretable as evidence of publication bias under heterogeneity of this magnitude. The qualitative synthesis identifies five dimensions associated with variation in these relationships: AI literacy and trust as preconditions for usefulness judgments; a shift from functional to identity-based acceptance shaped by pedagogical beliefs and institutional norms; the role of sociocultural and institutional context; tool-specific adoption logics; and ethical risk calibration as a values-based gate on adoption decisions. These findings suggest that predicting teacher AI adoption intentions may require variables beyond the TAM core, and motivate the development of extended frameworks designed for the sociotechnical complexity of AI in education.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Retrieval-augmented generation in biomedicine: a survey of technologies, datasets, and clinical applications

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11743-y · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

Large language models (LLMs) in biomedicine face a fundamental conflict between static parameter knowledge and the dynamic nature of clinical evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) addresses this by grounding generation in external data, yet it introduces new complexities in latency and architecture. This survey synthesizes the biomedical RAG landscape from 2020 to 2025 through a structured literature mapping of 178 screened records, yielding 94 representative studies classified into naive RAG (38 studies, 40.4%), advanced RAG (46 studies, 48.9%), and modular RAG (10 studies, 10.7%). Beyond a technological taxonomy, we formalize the biomedical RAG trilemma, identifying the inherent trade-offs between reasoning depth, inference latency, and data privacy that constrain current clinical deployment. We analyze how recent agentic workflows enhance diagnostic reasoning but risk prohibitive latency, and how privacy constraints dictate the choice between powerful cloud-based models and local deployment. Finally, we outline the alignment gap in multimodal RAG and propose future directions for self-correcting, verifiable clinical agents.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

On the robustness verification of binary neural networks

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11661-z · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

Binary neural networks (BNNs) combine strong efficiency gains with a highly discrete structure that gives rise to distinctive robustness and verification challenges. This survey provides a dedicated overview of formal verification methods for BNNs, focusing on robustness properties, threat models, and the trade-offs between exactness, scalability, and strength of guarantees. We organize the literature according to the main verification paradigms proposed in this setting, including SAT/SMT-based methods, optimization-based approaches, reachability analysis, and quantitative or model-counting techniques. We discuss the main ideas behind these approaches, the guarantees they provide, and the practical challenges that remain in verifying BNNs at scale.

摘要（可展开，供朗读/NotebookLM）

论文题名

Enabling spatial intelligence in the AEC lifecycle: a framework and review of large language models

期刊：Artificial Intelligence Review · DOI：10.1007/s10462-026-11737-w · 摘要来源：账本已存摘要

The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry is undergoing a profound digital transformation driven by the urgent need to integrate fragmented, heterogeneous data into actionable intelligence. This paper provides a systematic review of 76 representative studies to examine how Large Language Models (LLMs) enable spatial intelligence across the entire building lifecycle. A layered spatial intelligence framework is proposed, encompassing the dimensions of design, construction, operation, as well as research and education. The review demonstrates that LLMs are evolving from passive text processors into active cognitive partners capable of semantic interpretation, spatial reasoning, and complex decision-making. Key findings highlight the effectiveness of LLMs in requirement translation, multimodal design generation, regulatory compliance, and lifecycle Building Information Modeling (BIM) integration. Despite these advancements, significant challenges persist regarding spatial reasoning accuracy, the lack of physical embodiment, and institutional data governance. This research outlines a strategic roadmap toward embodied intelligence, AEC-specific world models, and enhanced human-AI collaboration, providing a structured foundation for the advancement of LLM-driven spatial intelligence in professional practice.
